findings.where: Screen 5 (Two parts, two rules), SHOW text
findings.what: "Call the amounts a and b. Then a′ = −0.1a and b′ = −0.3b" skips the lesson's central step: A only stretches each eigenvector, so A(a(1, 2) + b(1, −2)) = −0.1a(1, 2) − 0.3b(1, −2), and each amount gets its own rate. A steps lesson shows only its screens, so Dan never sees why the equations come apart. Make room by cutting the two sentences about the (1, −2) line and keep the screen at about 90 words.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Two masses, two swings), SHOW text
findings.what: "The middle spring stretches by up to 4 cm, so ω² = 3k/m" skips the step that the stretch is twice each mass's shift, so each mass feels k from its outer spring and 2k from the middle one. The screen also never links B's eigenvalues 1 and 3 to ω² = (k/m)λ. At 94 words it is already over about 90, so drop "x₁ and x₂ are how far each sits right of its rest point" (the picture labels them) to make room.

findings.where: Screen 11 (Any start is a sum), SHOW text
findings.what: "The lines are at right angles, because (1, 1) · (−1, 1) = 0. So the shudder is two simple swings" makes the right angle the reason the motion splits, and that is wrong: the open tanks' (1, 2) and (1, −2) are not at right angles and still split. The split comes from writing the start as a sum of eigenvectors, so drop the "So" or give the right angle as a separate fact.

findings.where: Whole lesson against the brief (decisions and row 7)
findings.what: Four things the brief puts in lesson 7 appear on no screen and nowhere in explain or practice: complex eigenvalues coming back as Differential equations lesson 6's ringing, resonance when a drive nears a natural frequency (Differential equations lesson 7), and coupled circuits and the submarine dive model named as systems this method solves.

findings.where: Screen 3 (also 5, 7, 9, 11), System choice; 360 light and dark moved pictures
findings.what: From screen 3 the System choice offers Closed tanks and Two masses before either is taught. When another system is picked, the words keep describing the open tanks: the moved picture shows the (1, 1), λ = 0 line under text naming (1, 2) with −0.1. Dan can also run screen 13's answer early, so offer the choice later or add a line saying the words describe the open tanks.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Add the parts back), SHOW text
findings.what: "Then the two tanks match" reads as "afterwards" when it means "at that moment" (x₂′ = 0 exactly when 0.2x₁ = 0.2x₂). Also, "the larger eigenvalue takes over" needs "the one nearer zero", because −0.1 is the smaller in size, which is the opposite of the step rule quoted just before it.

At the full 40 g scale the bend onto the (1, 2) line happens inside one grid square of the origin. The claim "the trail bends onto the (1, 2) line" is hard to see until screen 8 zooms in after a right answer, so zoom at the end of screen 7's demonstration too.

Line breaks split "100 / L", "20 / L/min" and the equation "x₂′ = 0.2x₁ − / 0.2x₂", because code spans over 16 characters are not kept whole. Use non-breaking spaces between each number and its unit, and keep the short equation on one line.

"So the dot runs straight to (15, 15)" contradicts screen 6, which marks "0" wrong because a decay never quite reaches its end. The e^(−0.4t) part never fully dies, so say "straight towards (15, 15)".

The two line labels sit stacked at the top centre, "(−1, 1), ω ≈ 17.3 rad/s" above "(1, 1), ω = 10 rad/s". Neither is beside its own line's end, so it is not obvious at a glance which label names which line.

findings.where: Key under the plane, screens 5 and 9 (films s4 and s8)
findings.what: Key entries come and go mid-run, so legend items jump rows. On screen 5 the parts entries fade in and push "eigenvector line" and "1 square = 10 g" onto a new row in the first half second. On screen 9 "a + b" shows only during the glide at about 2.2 s. Reserve the key slots from the start.
No screen checks the eigenvalues −0.1 and −0.3. At 68 words, screen 3 has room for "They add to the trace, −0.4, and multiply to the determinant, 0.03."

findings.where: Steps flow as a whole (screen 11 or the finish panel)
findings.what: Where Dan meets this never reaches a screen. The propulsion shaft (discs as masses, shaft lengths as springs, natural frequencies as square roots of eigenvalues) is only in the practice text, which a steps lesson does not show. One sentence on a screen or in the finish panel would make the point land.

findings.where: interactive.whatAmILookingAt (printed in the dossier under "What you're looking at")
findings.what: It ends with build notes rather than teaching: "A short lesson in thirteen small screens", "Each idea screen's words stay within about 90 words" and "On a narrow phone the answers and the readouts wrap". It also says each tank's grams are drawn beside it, but the pictures show only the x₁ and x₂ labels.
